title: What is known about 1RB0RD_0RC1RE_1RD0LA_1LE1LC_1RF0LD_---0RA
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RD_0RC1RE_1RD0LA_1LE1LC_1RF0LD_---0RA.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.

Its whole run is now known to be the orbit of an explicit map on two numbers, proved in Lean: a stack of m words 1011 and a block of n ones. The block grows like 8n/3 each phase while the stack loses one or two words; when the stack runs out the machine either halts or rebuilds a much larger stack and starts again. Whether it halts is a question about the residues mod 3 of a Collatz-like sequence, of the same kind as the famous cryptid Antihydra.
verdict: The question is open, and reduced to a Collatz-like map (kernel). Lean proves that the machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of (14, 5) under the map next below reaches a point (1, n) with n % 3 = 1 (halts_iff, lean/Map.lean).

The first two cycles do not halt. The orbit resets at phases 8 and 6,819; at phase 6,819 the stack has more than 102900 words, so the machine runs at least 102899 steps without halting (runs_long, lean/Orbit.lean, by native_decide). Deciding the third cycle needs about 5·102901 phases of the map: out of reach by simulation.

Heuristically it halts, absurdly late. If the residues mod 3 behave like coin flips, each cycle ends in a halt with probability 1/5 (simulated: 0.19 to 0.20 over 4,000 random cycles from large random starts), so the machine halts with probability 1, but each cycle is exponentially longer than the one before: a halt would come after a tower of exponentials of steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 105,361 cells have been visited and 82,022 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The phase start and the map
claims.text: A phase start is P m n = 0^inf (1011)^m 1^n (10)^3 A> 1 0^inf. Writing n = 3k + 3 + r with r < 3, from P m n the machine reaches: for r = 0, P (m-1) (8k+19) if m ≥ 1 and P (2k+4) 5 if m = 0; for r = 1, P (m-2) (8k+29) if m ≥ 2, a halt if m = 1, P 0 (8k+18) if m = 0; for r = 2, P (m-2) (8k+35) if m ≥ 2, P (2k+8) 5 if m = 1, P 0 (8k+18) if m = 0. Each case is a chain of symbolic runs proved step by step plus an induction over the inner bouncer.

claims.title: Blank tape reaches P 14 5
claims.text: After 1,098 steps from blank tape the configuration is P 14 5.

claims.title: The reduction
claims.text: The machine halts from blank tape if and only if the orbit of (14, 5) under next reaches a point (1, n) with n % 3 = 1.

claims.title: Two cycles without a halt; no halt in 10<sup>2899</sup> steps
claims.text: Compiled evaluation of the map shows the orbit at phase 6,819 is (M, 5) with M > 102900 (2,902 digits). Each later phase removes at most two words of the stack and the map can only stop at m = 1, so the next 102899 phases exist, and the machine does not halt in its first 102899 steps.

claims.title: The map against the machine
claims.text: Simulating the machine from P m n for 598 pairs (all m ≤ 7 with 3 ≤ n < 59, and 150 random pairs up to m = 60, n = 400) gives the next phase start the map predicts, or a halt exactly at m = 1, n ≡ 1 (mod 3); the run from blank tape passes through the phase starts the map predicts up to step 3.6·109. (Lean proves the map for all values; this is an independent check.)

claims.title: Halting probability 1/5 per cycle
claims.text: Within a cycle the stack drops by 2 (when r ≠ 0) or 1 (r = 0); if the residues are like fair dice the stack lands on 1 with probability 3/5, and then halts with probability 1/3: 1/5 per cycle. Simulating 4,000 cycles of the map from random large starts gives 0.19 to 0.20. The machine would then halt with probability 1, but cycle c+1 is about (8/3)^(m_c/1.8) times longer than cycle c.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Equivalent to: does the orbit of (14, 5) under next ever reach (1, n) with n ≡ 1 (mod 3)? The third cycle starts with a stack of about 8.3·102901 words and is out of reach of computation; nothing like a proof for the residues is in sight (it is a Collatz-type question).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows, and now we know exactly why. Lean proves that this machine's whole run is the orbit of a two-number map: a block of ones grows by a factor of about 8/3 each phase while a stack of 1011 words drains. It halts only if the stack runs out in one particular way, a residue question about a Collatz-like sequence. Twice it has not; the third chance comes after about 102901 phases.

facts.text: The run from blank tape is the orbit of an explicit map, proved in Lean.
No halt: two full cycles of the map evaluated by compiled code.
Chance that a cycle ends in a halt, if residues are random.

sections.heading: A stack, a block, and a bouncer
html: Every so often the tape has exactly this shape, a phase start P m n: on the left a stack of m copies of the word 1011, then a solid block of n ones, then 101010 with the head (state A) on a 1 at the right end.

<svg viewBox="0 0 560 120" role="img" aria-label="the phase-start tape" style="width:100%;max-width:560px;height:auto;font:12px var(--mono);">
<rect x="10" y="30" width="200" height="34" fill="var(--accent)" opacity="0.25"/><text x="110" y="52" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--fg)">(1011)^m  stack</text>
<rect x="215" y="30" width="230" height="34" fill="var(--head)" opacity="0.25"/><text x="330" y="52" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--fg)">1^n  block</text>
<rect x="450" y="30" width="80" height="34" fill="var(--line)" opacity="0.6"/><text x="490" y="52" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--fg)">101010</text>
<text x="536" y="52" fill="var(--fg)">A>1</text>
<text x="330" y="90" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--muted)">each round: 3 ones eaten here, four 10s added there →</text>
<text x="110" y="90" text-anchor="middle" fill="var(--muted)">end of phase: 1 or 2 words used</text>
</svg>

During a phase the head bounces at the right end. Each round it bites three ones off the block and adds four copies of 10 at the right, so after about n/3 rounds the block is gone and there are about 4n/3 copies of 10. Then one long sweep turns every 10 into 11: the new block has about 8n/3 ones. Meanwhile the left end of the block has bitten into the stack and used up one or two words 1011, depending on what was left over (n mod 3).

sections.heading: The map, case by case
html: Write n = 3k + 3 + r with r = 0, 1 or 2. From P m n the machine reaches:
Every entry is a theorem in Lean (next_reach, halts_P1); together with the start (P 14 5 after 1,098 steps) this gives halts_iff: the machine halts exactly when the orbit reaches the bold cell.
A reset happens when the stack is empty: the sweep pairs the copies of 10 into a brand-new stack of about 2n/3 words, and the block restarts at 5 ones.

sections.heading: Cycles, each astronomically longer than the last
html: From blank tape the orbit starts at (14, 5). The stack of 14 drains in 8 phases (block: 5, 35, 115, 325, 885, 2371, 6341, 16931) and ends at m = 1 with r = 2: a reset, to a stack of 11,292 words, at step 445,346,602.

That stack drains in 6,811 phases, while the block grows to 2,903 digits. It ends at m = 0: a reset again, to a stack of about 8.3·102901 words. Draining that takes some 5·102901 phases, and nobody can compute that far. Lean checks the two cycles (by compiled evaluation) and concludes that the machine runs at least 102899 steps without halting.

So the question is whether some future cycle ends in the bold cell, m = 1 with r = 1. If the residues mod 3 behave like dice, a cycle ends that way with probability 1/5, and the machine eventually halts with probability 1, after a tower of exponentials of steps. This is the same kind of question as for the cryptid Antihydra: easy to state, hopeless to prove with current mathematics.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.534).
After 109 steps the tape spans 105,361 cells (7 left of the start, 69,796 right), with a density of 1s of 0.778.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

family: Collatz-like map with a draining counter (Antihydra-like)
summary: Kernel-proved reduction to a map on two numbers: a block n grows like 8n/3 while a stack m of 1011s drains by 1 or 2 per phase; halts iff the stack runs out at m=1 with n ≡ 1 (mod 3). Two cycles pass without halting; the third needs about 10^2901 phases.
